title: fix(plugin-auth): os migrate apply's account-issuer pre-flight names each colliding row's stored issuer
body:
Fixes #25030

Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What was wrong

When the `sys_account.issuer` retirement pre-flight finds a `(provider_id, account_id)` key held by more than one row, `os migrate apply --allow-destructive` refuses to drop `sys_account.issuer` and prints the pre-flight's report. That report labelled every colliding row's issuer `(none)`. `os migrate account-issuer` printed the stored values for the same database. The issuers are what an operator needs to decide which row survives.

Cause: `probeAccountIdentityCollisions` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-identity-preflight.ts`) read through whatever `find` it was handed. `apply`'s gate handed it the `objectql` engine, whose read verbs answer declared columns only, and the shipped `sys_account` no longer declares `issuer`. `account-issuer.ts` handed it a reader of its own over the driver (`getDriverForObject`). So the two doors ran one probe over two readers, and the readers disagreed.

### Reproduced first, at `d68aab6fde`, on the built CLI

The fixture is a SQLite copy. The driver built `sys_account` from today's object. Then the legacy `issuer` column was added and the `(provider_id, account_id)` unique was dropped. Two rows, `acc_dup` and `acc_two`, share `credential / usr_25030`, with stored issuers `https://idp-a.example` and `https://idp-b.example`. The app config declares `requires: ['auth']`, so `apply` composes the auth family.

| Door (exit) | Report at `d68aab6fde` | At this branch |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes` (1) | `credential / usr_25030 — 2 rows [acc_dup, acc_two], issuers [(none)], users [usr_25030]` | `… issuers [https://idp-a.example, https://idp-b.example], users [usr_25030]` |
| `os migrate apply … --json` (1) | `preflight.collisions[0].issuers: ["(none)"]` | `["https://idp-a.example","https://idp-b.example"]` |
| `os migrate account-issuer` (1) | `… issuers [https://idp-a.example, https://idp-b.example] …` | unchanged |

## The fix: one reader, owned by plugin-auth

- **The probe reads storage itself.** When its source offers the storage door (`getDriverForObject`, the `objectql` engine both CLI doors pass), `probeAccountIdentityCollisions` reads `sys_account` through the driver the engine routes that name to, and only through it. A missing driver refuses; the probe never falls back to the engine's `find`. The query is the one `account-issuer.ts` used to send: same columns, same keyset walk, no driver options. `apply`'s gate (`utils/apply-drop-gates.ts`) is untouched and now reports the stored issuers.
- **`os migrate account-issuer` adopts it.** The command passes its engine to the probe and deletes its own reader. Its missing-table reading (a database with no `sys_account` table reads as no rows) moves into the probe as an opt-in, `onTableAbsent`. A caller that passes it gets no rows and is told once. A caller that does not pass it is refused, as for any other failed read. No other `packages/cli` file is touched.
- **A source that offers `find` alone is still read as handed, as before.** No production caller does this any more. It is kept because `packages/cli/test/migrate-drop-gate-remedies.pin.test.ts` drives the real probe through a `find`-only fake engine, and that file is outside this card's fence. The open question in the dev report covers retiring that path.
- **Nothing else moves.** `sys_account` does not re-declare `issuer`, and nothing under `packages/spec` or `packages/objectql` changes.

## Unchanged, measured

**Public door, before and after.** The CLI was built at `d68aab6fde` and again at this branch (`turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/cli...'`). `account-issuer` and `apply --allow-destructive --yes`, human and `--json`, ran on five databases: issuer column with a collision, no issuer column with a collision, issuer column and clean, no `sys_account` table, and no database file. That is 20 runs per build. Their stdout and stderr were compared after normalising timestamps and timings.

- Exit codes are identical in all 20.
- 38 of the 40 streams are byte-identical. The two that differ are `apply`'s report on the issuer-column collision database, human and `--json`, and only on the issuers line shown above.
- With `preflight.collisions[].issuers` removed, the `--json` document equals the old one: the same `message: refused_account_issuer_collisions`, `ok`, keys, row ids, users and counts.
- `account-issuer` is byte-identical on all five databases, human and `--json`, including the no-table line and the no-file run.

These comparisons were measured twice: at `37077ac369`, an earlier strict-contract cut before the merge of `origin/main`, and at `010afefb70`, the merged head that this PR carries. Both builds compare against the same `d68aab6fde` baseline, with the same 20 exit codes and the same 38 identical streams. The card's own database was re-run at `010afefb70` with the result in the table above.

**Pins**, in a new file: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/account-identity-preflight-stored-issuer.test.ts`. They run on a real `SqlDriver` over a SQLite file that is built independently of the code under test. Each database is read three ways:

- through `apply`'s composition, with `sys_account` registered as it ships;
- through `account-issuer`'s composition, with `sys_account` unregistered;
- through a reference: the engine-`find` read the probe made before this change.

What they pin:

- **Stored issuers are named.** The colliding rows' stored issuers appear in the report and in its text. A premise check shows the engine read of the same database gives `(none)`.
- **One reader.** Both compositions give the same report and the same text.
- **The verdict is unchanged.** Every field except `issuers` equals the reference, and the refusal (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409) carries the same message. This also holds over a 1,200-row walk with the colliding rows on its first and last page. A clean table stays clean.
- **No `issuer` column.** A database without the column gives exactly the reference report (every row `(none)`) on both compositions.
- **Missing table.** With `onTableAbsent`, the probe reads no rows and tells the caller once. Without it, the probe refuses. When the table is present, the caller is never told it is absent.
- **No driver.** If the storage door yields no driver, the probe refuses and never calls the source's own `find`.

**Ablation**, one leg per pinned behaviour, on the committed fix through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. In every leg the anchor went from 1 hit to 0, the blob changed, and the run went red at the assertion of interest. Every restore was `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, proven by the blob equalling HEAD's and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The final `git status` was clean. The subject resolves through a relative `src/` import, so there is no `dist/` leg.

Every leg ran at `010afefb70`.

| Leg | Mutation | Red, and where |
|:--|:--|:--|
| L1 | the engine's `find` wins again whenever the source has one (the defect) | 7/10. The stored-issuer pin fails at its `toEqual` (issuers `(none)`). The one-reader pin, the multi-page pin, the no-column pin and two missing-table pins fail because `account-issuer`'s composition is refused `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`. The no-driver pin fails because the source's `find` is read. The verdict and clean-table pins stay green, as they should. |
| L2 | a reader that refuses rows without a stored `issuer` | 5/10. The no-column pin fails at its own probe call. The other four fail at their engine-read reference, which carries no `issuer` by construction. |
| L3 | collisions grouped by `issuer` too | 4/10. The verdict pin fails at `after.ok` (expected false, got true). The stored-issuer, one-reader and multi-page pins fail too. Before this fix the mutation was invisible, because `issuer` always read as undefined. |
| L4 | the `onTableAbsent` call removed | 1/10: "a caller that asks … is told once" (`told` 0) |
| L5 | a missing table softened without the opt-in | 1/10: "a caller that does not ask is refused" |
| L6 | no driver falls back to the source's `find` | 1/10: the no-driver pin |

## Verification

Every run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, with each exit captured before any pipe. Merged head `010afefb70`; the only later commit is changeset text, `652462c694`.

- **Build closures:** `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-auth^...' build` exit 0. `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/cli...'` exit 0 (61/61 tasks).
- **New pins:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/account-identity-preflight-stored-issuer.test.ts`, 10 passed.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`:** `Test Files 176 passed (176)`, `Tests 3348 passed | 10 skipped (3358)`.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`:** exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK`. Debt is unchanged at 10 files / 88 errors. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file once.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`:** exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- **CLI unit tier:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`, `Test Files 319 passed (319)`, `Tests 4730 passed (4730)`.
  - An earlier strict-contract cut of this branch reddened four cases in `test/migrate-drop-gate-remedies.pin.test.ts`. That file's fake engine offers `find` alone. Those reds are why the probe still reads a handed `find` source.
- **CLI integration:** `src/commands/migrate/apply.account-issuer-retirement.integration.test.ts` was run locally because `account-issuer`'s read moved: `Tests 4 passed (4)`. The rest of the integration tier is declared to CI.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `652462c694` derived 72 commands.
  - 70 exited 0.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: untouched packages have no `dist/`). After a full `turbo run build` (76/76 tasks, exit 0), both exited 0 on the same head: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads — 112 published require entry point(s) across 69 package(s) load`, and `check-i18n-coverage: OK (14 config(s), 621 baselined untranslated string(s), none new)`.
  - `--ran` over the first record: `72 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 70 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`. Over the record with the two re-runs: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 72 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 72 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 72 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).`
  - Every family CI runs is read from this PR's check-runs, not re-run here.

## Acceptance notes

- **Published surface.** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` gains:
  - two exported types, `AccountTableStorage` (`getDriverForObject`) and `AccountTableDriver`;
  - one option, `AccountIdentityPreflightOptions.onTableAbsent`.

  `probeAccountIdentityCollisions` now takes `AccountTableStorage | AccountIdentityReadEngine`, so every earlier caller still type-checks. The dispatch's `Clause-②: no` is kept as given. The dev report asks whether these additions are "public surface" under the clause.
- **Unreachable wording delta in `account-issuer`.** If the booted stack had no `objectql` service at all, the refusal used to read `no driver serves sys_account on this stack`. It now reads `no readable ObjectQL engine`. Both are refusals with exit 1. `bootSchemaStack` always composes `objectql`, so this path is not reachable today. Where an engine is present but has no driver for the table, the old wording is unchanged.
- **Stale measurement row.** `find-envelope-limb-removal.test.ts` row B9 still measures an engine `find` of `sys_account` as "the exact read" of this site. The site now reads the driver. `SqlDriver.find` declares an array of rows as its answer, and the probe still refuses a non-array. The row stays green; it is outside the file surface, so it is left as is.
- **Merged `origin/main` before opening.** The merge (`eddffc3390`) was clean. The incoming commits touch `packages/spec` translations, `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-extract.ts` and its tests, `core`, `lint` and `rest`, and none of them touch this diff's files. Everything under Verification was re-run on the merged head.

One bullet names the widened surface: `AccountTableStorage`, `AccountTableDriver`, `AccountIdentityPreflightOptions.onTableAbsent`, and the probe's `AccountTableStorage | AccountIdentityReadEngine` source. `@objectstack/cli` stays patch.
